title: Levelwise isomorphisms and complete cones
statement:
Fix the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] on $T_{\Proet}$, with $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and $P_n=A/I^n$. All derived categories of coefficients below are categories of $A_T$-module sheaves, and every finite reduction means $K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, regarded as an $A_T$-module object by restriction of scalars. Derived completeness means that the Koszul completion map of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is an isomorphism.

A morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ whose evaluation at every $n$ is an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism and remains an isomorphism after $\Rlim$. If a derived complete object $C$ satisfies $C\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T=0$ for every $n$, then $C=0$. Consequently a morphism between derived complete objects is an isomorphism once every finite reduction is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Let $u:M_\bullet\to N_\bullet$ have isomorphic derived evaluations and complete it to a distinguished triangle with third term $E_\bullet$. The exact evaluations of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] extend as triangulated functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. At each level compare the evaluated triangle with the triangle $M_n\xrightarrow{1}M_n\to0\to M_n[1]$: the first two components $1,u_n$ are isomorphisms, hence [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $0\to E_n$ an isomorphism. Since kernels and cokernels in the tower category are levelwise, $\operatorname{ev}_nH^j(E_\bullet)=H^j(E_n)=0$ for all $n,j$, so every $H^j(E_\bullet)$ is the zero tower. A representing complex of $E_\bullet$ is therefore acyclic and its map from the zero complex is a quasi-isomorphism; localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $E_\bullet=0$. Comparing the original triangle with the identity triangle and applying the same triangle lemma to components $1,0\to E_\bullet$ now shows $u$ is an isomorphism.

The functor $\Rlim:D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))\to D(T_{\Proet},A)$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] sends an inverse of $u$ to an inverse of $\Rlim u$, by its identity and composition laws. This proves the derived-limit assertion in the same coefficient category.

Write $R(K)=\Rlim K_\bullet$, where $K_\bullet$ is the strict $A_T$-linear quotient reduction tower. This completion functor carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles. Indeed [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] applies on the single site $T_{\Proet}$ to each projection $A_T\to(P_n)_T$, giving the exact reduction functor computed on K-flat resolutions [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For a cone triangle of an original chain map $f_0$, use the functorial K-flat resolutions fixed in the adic datum to obtain a chain map $f:P\to Q$ and a commuting square of quasi-isomorphisms to $f_0$. The induced cone map is a quasi-isomorphism: after localization the two resolution maps are isomorphisms, and [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] gives an isomorphism on the third terms. Thus every distinguished triangle admits this K-flat cone model. For the resulting quasi-isomorphism $h:\operatorname{Cone}(f)\to\operatorname{Cone}(f_0)$, functoriality of the fixed resolutions gives $Qh$; the commuting resolution square makes $Qh$ a quasi-isomorphism by two-out-of-three on cohomology. Clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the levelwise cohomology calculation of step 1 then make its reductions an isomorphism of derived towers. Hence replacing the original cone by this model also preserves its chosen reduction tower. On the map $f:P\to Q$ the cone is K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum], and tensoring its matrix differential gives the chain isomorphism $\operatorname{Cone}(f)\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T\cong\operatorname{Cone}(f\otimes1)$. These identifications commute with every quotient transition: on both summands the transition is tensor with $(P_{n+1})_T\to(P_n)_T$, and the off-diagonal differential is $f\otimes1$. Thus they give a cone triangle in the strict tower category. To compare its third term with the chosen reduction tower of $\operatorname{Cone}(f)$, apply the fixed K-flat resolution to this cone. Its resolution map $Q(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes. By clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], tensoring this map with each $(P_n)_T$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The maps commute with quotient transitions because each is induced by this single resolution map. Their cone tower has zero cohomology at every evaluation, so the levelwise kernel/cokernel calculation of step 1 makes this comparison a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes. It therefore identifies the chosen reduction tower with the strict cone tower in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$. Distinguished triangles are the images of cone triangles up to isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so this calculation on K-flat models proves exactness of the reduction-tower functor. Applying the triangulated functor of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] proves the claim about $R$. The compatible maps $P\to P\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, commute with the cone inclusion and projection on the two summands; hence the completion units form a morphism from any distinguished triangle to its $R$-image, including the shifted last square.

For a derived complete $C$, [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] identifies its completion unit with an isomorphism $C\to R(C)$. If every $C\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ is zero, step 1 applied to $0\to C_\bullet$ makes $C_\bullet$ the zero object of the derived tower category. The triangulated (in particular additive) functor [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] sends the zero object to zero: its identity becomes the zero endomorphism by additivity. Thus $R(C)=0$ and $C=0$.

For $u:C\to D$ with complete source and target, let $E$ be its cone. Step 3 gives a morphism of distinguished triangles $(C,D,E)\to(R(C),R(D),R(E))$ whose first two components are the completion units, isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction]. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], $E\to R(E)$ is an isomorphism. The same reconstruction proposition identifies this map with the Koszul completion map through its functorial isomorphism $E^\wedge_{\mathrm{Kos}}\cong R(E)$. Hence $E\to E^\wedge_{\mathrm{Kos}}$ is an isomorphism, precisely derived completeness by [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. This proves cone closure inside $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ without any constant-coefficient comparison.

Suppose every reduction of $u:C\to D$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], reduction carries the cone triangle to a distinguished triangle. Map the identity triangle on $C\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$ to this reduced triangle, with first two components the identity and the reduction of $u$; the triangle axiom supplies the third component from zero. The first two components are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the third component an isomorphism and gives $E\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T=0$ for every $n$. The cone is complete by step 5, and step 4 therefore gives $E=0$. The morphism from the identity triangle on $C$ to the original triangle has components $1_C,u,0\to E$. Its first and third components are now isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $u$ an isomorphism.
